page.text:
Restricted quantifiers are abbreviations whose expansions expose their
logic. The formula $\forall x\in D\,P(x)$ means
$\forall x\,(x\in D\Rightarrow P(x))$, whereas $\exists x\in D\,P(x)$
means $\exists x\,(x\in D\land P(x))$. The different connective is
essential: using implication in the existential form would make any
object outside $D$ a vacuous witness.
